newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF's Marchelli sees room for manoeuvre on rates.
newsitem.headline: BoF's Marchelli sees room for manoeuvre on rates.

text.p: Bank of France council member Paul Marchelli repeated in a magazine interview that he saw room for manoeuvre on interest rates but market conditions had to be right to allow France to ease further.
"Of course there is room for manoeuvre," he said in an interview to be published in weekly magazine Investir on Saturday.
"I think that the monetary policy of recent months will continue," he said. The Bank of France has been steadily but slowly lowering official short-term rates over recent months.
Marchelli said that any acceleration or deceleration in this process would depend on other factors than changes earlier this month to the membership of the monetary policy council.
These other factors would include the stability of the franc.

French President Jacques Chirac earlier this month appointed two men close to him to the nine-member council, replacing two outgoing members who had been seen as staunch supporters of the Bank's policy of giving priority to defending the stability of the franc against the mark.

Economists said the appointments might prompt a slightly faster pace of rate cuts at the Bank, which has tended to follow German rate cuts and maintain a premium over German rates to cushion the franc against any attack on currency markets.

Asked whether the Bank of France could cut rates below German rates, Marchelli said, "One can consider everything. But once again, the conditions have to be in place for markets to accept that our move corresponds to the reality of our economy and the strength of our currency."
